title: "Unacknowledged special access": The Age of Disclosure director explains how UFO crash retrieval is being "hidden from congressional oversight"

content:
The Age of Disclosure director Dan Farah explained how UFO crash retrieval programs were allegedly being concealed from congressional oversight. While speaking with Dr. Mayim Bialik, Dan described the UFO crash retrieval as an unacknowledged special access program. Dan said,

"It's a program that's been hidden from congressional oversight, hidden from presidents, and hidden from the public. It's essentially an unacknowledged special access program."

The director explained that officials discovered a highly secretive UAP crash retrieval operation known as the legacy program. Dan said that whenever a UAP crash was reported, whether in the United States or another country, teams connected to the program were sent to recover the craft and transport it to a secure location.

Dan said that he didn't know where those locations were. He claimed that the recovered crafts were allegedly taken to a safe facility where other parts of the program work to reverse engineer the technology.

Continue reading more about the story.

A chat with Dr. Mayim Bialik: Dan Farah revealed claims about the secret UFO Crash Retrieval Program

Dan revealed that several people featured in The Age of Disclosure said that they had found a highly secretive UAP crash retrieval and reverse-engineering program that had reportedly existed since the 1940s. He explained that the program had allegedly been kept hidden from congressional oversight, withheld from presidents, and concealed from the public.

The director also explained the four main elements of the legacy program. He said,

"The people I interviewed all revealed that the program has the ability to access the tools of many other elements of government, but the four main elements of the legacy program are the CIA, the Air Force, the Department of Energy, and major US defense contractors."

Dan explained that since the UFO emits significant amounts of energy, there's definitely a connection with the Air Force and nuclear energy experts.

Dan Farah explained why it was easier for DOE to hide the information

While speaking with Dr. Mayim, Dan claimed that the Department of Energy, or DOE, has a classification system that is more restrictive than those used by the broader intelligence community. So, it became easier for the department to hide the information. Dan said,

"But the other thing is the Department of Energy has a classification system that is much stronger than the regular intelligence community. So they can hide information easier."

Dan also explained that defense contractors include aerospace engineers, physicists, and other specialists with the technical expertise to reverse engineer advanced technology. He said these experts can receive pieces of recovered craft and study them to understand how the technology works. They then try to recreate or copy that technology. The director finally said that major companies, including Lockheed Martin, were often linked to these efforts.
